newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Drought may boost Cyprus grain imports.
newsitem.headline: Drought may boost Cyprus grain imports.

text.p: Prolonged drought in Cyprus is likely to cut local barley production and boost imports, a grain official said on Tuesday.
"In a good year the (local) production is normally around 180,000 metric tonnes and in a bad year 120,000," said Andreas Gavrielides, Trade and Administrative Officer at the Cyprus Grains Commission.
"This year production could be lower than 100,000 because there is no rain at all," he told Reuters.
This January has been the driest this century, with rainfall averaging 8 mm compared to a normal 102 mm.

The Cyprus Grain Commission, (CGC) a semi-government organisation, is Cyprus's sole importer of grain. On average it imports around 350,000 tonnes of barley a year, 120,000 tonnes of corn, and 90,000 tonnes of wheat, comprising a mixture of durum, spring and soft wheat.

Gavrielides said the island's barley needs this year could reach 400,000 tonnes because of drought and reduced fodder output, coupled with increased food demand from tourism. Around two million tourists visit the eastern Mediterranean island each year.
The island grows no corn and very little wheat.
The Grain Commission subsidises the sale price of barley and corn. Animal feed is subsidised so it will not have adverse effects on local livestock breeders.
"The animal industry needs to feed animals at low cost otherwise it will not be competitive," said Gavrielides. "The sector must be given benefits to keep it alive."

Gavrielides said the grain commission was currently extending its silo capacity to 160,000 tonnes from the present 120,000 tonnes, and did not rule out the possibility of a deregulation of grain imports in the future.

"Maybe after a transitional period there will be some kind of deregulation," he said, adding that decision rested with the government. "But we will remain active to stabilise the prices and quality of the grain."
